learning_outcomes.text: Students who have successfully completed this module are able to name the necessity of using high voltages in electrical power supply and to select the optimal transmission voltage.
Dimension, test and diagnose insulation systems.
Describe and classify environmental and economic aspects of the subject area.

After completing the module, students can safely describe and apply high voltage engineering methods (insulation coordination, stress and behavior of insulating materials, testing and diagnosis) to electrical energy systems.
Different approaches for insulation systems can be contrasted and compared.
Students design insulation systems after analyzing the anticipated stresses and create equivalent circuit diagrams and test/diagnosis plans from them.
From these, scientifically sound decisions for the development of the insulation system are made and applied and verified in the high voltage laboratory.
Graduates of the High Voltage Technology module derive, explain, and justify research questions on partial discharge measurement technology in the practical course and propose solutions.
Students critically analyze and evaluate insulation systems with regard to their feasibility, safety, and economic efficiency.
They can competently and clearly present and communicate the results.

Graduates develop a professional self-image that is oriented towards the goals and standards of professional action in professional fields primarily outside of academia and can assess their own abilities.
They autonomously reflect on subject-related design and decision-making freedoms and use them under guidance.
They also critically reflect on their professional actions in relation to societal expectations and consequences.

syllabus_topics: High Voltage Generation for Testing Purposes
assessment_rules: The graded examination is an oral exam (30 minutes, covering all topics from lectures and practicals) or a written exam (duration according to the applicable study regulations). The ungraded examination is experimental work, consisting of approximately 6 experiments.
